audit.why: 49.77% over 2811 games is a genuine coin-flip, and the content layer already frames it as an early-Sion / late-Vladimir lane. No difficulty field exists to correct — the full layer for this matchup is absent entirely.

win[] reads Skill, Skill, Sion, Skill, Sion, Sion, Vladimir and matches the packet level chart row for row. Sion at 3 and 6 is right (full kit, then a gap-closer Vladimir has no dash to answer), and Vladimir at 2+ items is right given Crimson Pact turns his AP into HP.

audit.whatIsWrong: Sanguine Pool was quoted as a 22-second cooldown in the level-3 window and in the early-game text. 22s is rank 3; at level 3 Vladimir has it at rank 1, which is 28 seconds. Also missing: Riot's description states charged Tides of Blood is blocked by enemy units, which is the whole reason to trade from behind the wave.
audit.why: The bait-the-pool pattern is built on the wait, so a six-second error changes when the punish window actually opens.
audit.corrected: Cooldown corrected to 28s at rank 1; unit-blocking on Tides of Blood written into whys[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing on the page mentioned Grievous Wounds, despite Vladimir healing from Transfusion, Sanguine Pool and Hemoplague.
audit.why: Every extended trade and every all-in in this lane is decided by whether his sustain is cut; the first-item window is where that decision lands.
audit.corrected: Bramble Vest / Grievous Wounds timing added at the first-item spike and to the early-game plan.

edits.before: W-shield absorbs his E poke in short trades and your HP passive gets a minion stack — bait his pool by walking up with a half-charged Q, then back off to reset the cooldown clock.
edits.after: W-shield absorbs his E poke, and Riot's own text says charged Tides of Blood is blocked by enemy units — keep minions between you and trade from behind the wave, never in the open.

edits.before: Full kit online: fake the charged-Q approach to force pool, wait out the 22-second cooldown, then stun him into E armor-shred for a real kill window.
edits.after: Full kit online: fake the charged-Q approach to force pool — Sanguine Pool is 28s at rank 1 — then stun him into E armor-shred for a real kill window.

edits.before: Heartsteel + your kill-stack HP passive makes you nearly unkillable in short trades; Vladimir's first Rylai's gives him a slow but no real kill threat on you yet.
edits.after: Heartsteel bulk arrives, but so does his sustain — Bramble Vest here puts Grievous Wounds on Transfusion and Hemoplague before Rylai's makes his trades unwinnable.

edits.before: Build MR second item and plan for it early — Vladimir's E poke is AP and your W-shield does not stop it, so eating three E's in a row costs you a chunk of HP you will not get back in trades. The key level 1-3 pattern is telegraphing a charged Q to bait his pool, then walking up again once the 22-second cooldown ticks down and landing the real charge for the stun into E armor-shred. His Q drain during your W-shield window barely breaks even, so short trades where you land W-shield then immediately back off are slightly in your favour. Never let him stack three E pokes in a row unopposed — that is when his sustain edge shows up.
edits.after: Build MR second item and plan for it early — Vladimir's E poke is AP and your W-shield does not stop it, so eating three E's in a row costs you a chunk of HP you will not get back in trades. The key level 1-3 pattern is telegraphing a charged Q to bait his pool, then walking up again once the 28-second cooldown ticks down and landing the real charge for the stun into E armor-shred. His Q drain during your W-shield window barely breaks even, so short trades where you land W-shield then immediately back off are slightly in your favour. Never let him stack three E pokes unopposed, and buy Grievous Wounds early — sustain is how he wins.
